title: A continuous map from a profinite group to a discrete space is invariant under an open normal subgroup
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group and let $S$ be a discrete topological space. If $f:G\to S$ is continuous, then there is an open normal subgroup $U\subseteq G$ such that $f(xu)=f(x)$ for all $x\in G$ and $u\in U$.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous, the remark that continuity into a discrete space is equivalent to open stabilizers; the profinite compactness and open-normal-basis argument is supplied by the agent

proof.text: For each $s\in S$, the fibre $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is open because $S$ is discrete and $f$ is continuous. Thus the fibres form an open cover of the compact space $G$. For every $x\in G$, choose an open subgroup $V_x$ with $xV_x\subseteq f^{-1}(\{f(x)\})$, using that open subgroups form a neighbourhood basis at the identity in a profinite group: writing $G=\lim_iG_i$ as a cofiltered limit of finite discrete groups (the definition of a profinite group), the sets $p_i^{-1}(p_i(y))$ for the projections $p_i:G\to G_i$ form a basis of the topology because the limit is cofiltered, and $p_i^{-1}(p_i(e))=\ker p_i$ is an open normal subgroup; apply this to the open neighbourhood $x^{-1}f^{-1}(\{f(x)\})$ of $e$. A finite subcover $x_1V_{x_1},\ldots,x_rV_{x_r}$ exists. The intersection $V=\bigcap_{i=1}^rV_{x_i}$ is open, and if $x\in x_iV_{x_i}$ then $xV\subseteq x_iV_{x_i}$, so $f(xv)=f(x)$ for all $x\in G$ and $v\in V$.

source.place: Tag 04JP, label definition-G-module-continuous; the profinite compactness argument supplied by the agent

proof.text: An open subgroup $V$ of the compact group $G$ has finite index, since its cosets form a disjoint open cover of $G$, so the intersection of its finitely many conjugates, $U=\bigcap_{i=1}^r g_iVg_i^{-1}$ over representatives of $G/V$, is open and normal and is contained in $V$. Therefore $f(xu)=f(x)$ for every $x\in G$ and $u\in U$, because the equality from the first step holds for every element of $V$.
